tasks.title: Show each agent on the canvas: a named cursor that moves to what it edits, and a flash on every write
tasks.body:
Today nothing on the canvas shows that an agent is working or what it just changed. The only signals are a toast ("Applied N live MCP edit(s)") and the selection moving to inserted roots (`live_patch_apply.rs`).

## Behaviour
- **Agent cursor.** Each agent session (one per agent tab) gets a colour and a label (agent name, or agent and model).
  - The cursor appears when the session's first write lands. It moves to the next written node and settles near the middle of that node's bounds, at the nearest point inside the view.
  - Movement is an exponential follow with decay rate 2.5/s. Fade-in is 200 ms ease-out-cubic. After 5 s with no writes it fades out over 1.5 s.
  - Size setting: Hidden / Small 24 px / Medium 40 px / Large 56 px. Default Small, labelled with the agent name (pending owner ruling).
- **Write flash.** Every agent insert, update or replace flashes the node's outline in the agent's colour.
  - Envelope: attack 200 ms, hold 400 ms, release 300 ms. Stroke 2 px, or 1 px for inserts.
  - Top-level frames are not flashed.
  - When the cursor had to travel to the node, the flash starts 300 ms later so it lands with the cursor.
- **New top-level nodes** fade in from opacity 0 (decay 5/s) instead of popping in.
- **Several agents** (#572) each have their own colour and cursor.
- **Idle cost.** Animation frames are requested only while a cursor or flash is animating. When everything has settled, idle CPU returns to 0% (CLAUDE.md §4 idle invariants). Viewport-only work: no `app.changed()`, no `TileView::rev` bump.
- **Headless renders and exports** never contain cursors or flashes.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A stub agent writing three nodes shows one cursor travelling to each node and three flashes in its colour.
2. Two concurrent agents show two colours.
3. 5 s after the last write the cursor is gone, and a 20 s idle window measures 0.00% CPU (`ps -o time=` method from CLAUDE.md).
4. The size setting Hidden shows nothing.
5. A CPU export of the frame is pixel-identical with and without an active agent.

Load es-designer before UI code. Desktop capture at 1440 plus a short screen recording go in the PR (responsive: SKIPPED, owner default).

Depends on: #592 (in-progress flag), #572 (agent identity per run).

tasks.title: Agent tabs: live turn status, a 'worked for' receipt per turn, and a notification when an agent finishes in the background
tasks.body:
The session hooks already mark turn start and end (#647, #677). Use them so every agent tab shows what its agent is doing without reading the terminal.

## Behaviour
- **Status dot** on each agent tab and in the session dropdown:
  - running: animated;
  - needs input: the CLI waits for approval or an answer;
  - done, unread: the turn ended while the tab was not visible;
  - error;
  - stopped.
- **Status text** in the panel header while running. It shows the current tool step from the hook payload (for example "Editing 3 layers…"). With no tool step it shows "Working…", and after 30 s "Still working…".
- **Turn receipt** after each turn: `Worked for 1m 20s · 12 tool calls · 7 layers changed`.
  - Duration is rounded up to whole seconds, minimum 1 s; `Ns` under a minute, else `Nm Ns`.
  - Clicking it opens the per-turn change summary of #677.
  - Counts come only from hook data. Never estimate.
- **Background notification.** When a turn ends and Studio is unfocused, or that tab is not visible, send one OS notification: "<agent name> finished in <file name>" (or "needs your input"). Clicking it focuses the window and the tab (default pending owner ruling).
- Codex tabs use the OSC/heuristic status that #677 uses.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A stub CLI that emits the hook events drives the dot through running → needs input → done.
2. The receipt shows the exact duration and counts from the hook payloads.
3. With Studio unfocused, one notification is sent per finished turn and none while focused on that tab.
4. Works for Claude, Codex, Grok and Antigravity tabs.

Load es-designer before UI code. Desktop capture at 1440 in the PR.

Depends on: #677 (turn grouping).

tasks.title: Stop an agent from the panel: interrupt the CLI, close its open edit batch as one undo step, and record that it was stopped
tasks.body:
There is no Stop control in the Agents panel chrome. Stopping means typing into the terminal.

## Behaviour
- **Stop button** in the panel header, shown while the tab's turn is running. Esc does the same while focus is in the panel chrome, not inside the terminal, where Esc belongs to the CLI.
  - It sends the CLI's own interrupt: Esc for TUIs that use it, otherwise Ctrl+C.
  - If the turn has not ended 3 s later, it sends Ctrl+C once more.
- On stop:
  - the turn's pending live edits are applied and closed as one undo step (same grouping as #589/#677);
  - in-progress flags on the agent's frames clear (#592);
  - the turn receipt reads `Stopped by you after 42s`.
- With parallel agents (#572), the header offers "Stop all" next to the per-tab Stop.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Stop on a stub CLI that writes in a loop ends the turn within 3 s.
2. The document holds every edit received before the stop, as one undo step.
3. No in-progress flag remains.
4. The receipt says it was stopped.
5. Esc inside the terminal still reaches the CLI unchanged.

Load es-designer before UI code. Desktop capture at 1440 in the PR.

Depends on: #589, #592, #677.

tasks.title: Cmd+Z and Shift+Cmd+Z undo document edits while an agent terminal has focus
tasks.body:
While the agent terminal has keyboard focus, Cmd+Z is swallowed:
- the shell returns early when the terminal captures the keyboard (`crates/designos-app/src/shell.rs:482-485`);
- the terminal key map has no Z (`terminal.rs:3520-3585`).

A user who watches an agent work in the terminal cannot undo its last edit without first clicking the canvas.

## Acceptance criteria
- Cmd+Z / Shift+Cmd+Z (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y on Windows and Linux) undo and redo the document while the terminal has focus.
  - On Windows and Linux, Ctrl+Z inside the terminal stays the shell's suspend key, unless the CLI is a full-screen TUI that does not use it.
  - Pick and document the rule; macOS uses Cmd and has no clash.
- The undo granularity is unchanged: one step per agent tool call, or per turn once #589 lands.
- Shell test: focus the terminal, apply a live agent edit, press Cmd+Z, and the edit is reverted.

Desktop capture or terminal capture in the PR.

tasks.title: Agent tabs: classify mid-session failures (rate limit, login expired, billing, server error, context full) and show the next action
tasks.body:
#650 and #673 cover a CLI that fails to start. Nothing explains a failure in the middle of a session: the tab only shows terminal text.

## Behaviour
- Classify from the hook payloads and the CLI's own error output (patterns kept as data per CLI). Classes: rate limited, login expired, billing or quota, provider server error, context window full, network offline.
- Show a banner above the terminal with one line in plain words and one action:
  - Wait and retry (shows the reset time when the CLI reports it);
  - Run login;
  - Open the provider's billing page;
  - Start a new session (context full);
  - Retry when online.
- After a provider server error, check that provider's public status page once and show its incident title if one is open. Never poll while idle.
- "Copy details" copies the CLI name and version, the class, the last 40 lines of output and the session id. It never includes tokens or keys; redact anything matching key patterns.
- Unknown failures show the last output lines and "Copy details". Never a made-up cause.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Stub CLIs emitting each class's known output show the matching banner and action.
2. An unknown error shows no class.
3. The copied details pass a redaction test with planted fake keys.

tasks.title: Agents panel accessibility: announce finished, needs-input and error states, and label the panel regions
tasks.body:
The Agents panel gives screen-reader users no signal when an agent finishes, waits for input or fails.

## Acceptance criteria
- Through egui's AccessKit integration, a turn ending, a tab needing input, and an error each produce one polite announcement: "<agent> finished", "<agent> needs your input", "<agent> failed: <class>".
- The panel, tab strip, terminal and composer are labelled regions. Every icon button has an accessible name: Send, Stop, New session, Close tab, Selection chip.
- Keyboard: a shortcut moves focus to the composer and back to the canvas (documented in the shortcuts list).
- Test with the AccessKit tree in a shell test: the announcement node appears when a stub turn ends.

tasks.title: Agents panel empty state: sample prompts that send a real prompt, and attach hints
tasks.body:
The empty state ("What's next?" category cards, `terminal.rs:2604-2630`) today leads to template actions (#681).

## Behaviour
- Up to 6 sample prompts written for the open file's context: no selection, a frame selected, or an empty file.
  - Clicking one puts the prompt in the composer, focused, for the user to edit or send. It never sends by itself.
  - Prompts are data (a TOML list), so they can change without code.
- One hint line: how to send the selection (#654) and how to @-mention layers (#655).
- When no agent CLI is installed, the empty state shows the install guidance from #652 instead of sample prompts.

## Acceptance criteria
The three contexts show their prompts. A click fills the composer and makes no canvas change. The no-CLI state shows install guidance.

Load es-designer before UI code. Desktop capture at 1440 in the PR.

Depends on: #681.

tasks.title: Agent composer: send into the tab's live CLI session, with prompt history and a draft per tab
tasks.body:
Each composer message today starts a new one-shot CLI call (`claude -p`, `codex exec`, `grok -p`, `agy -p`; `build_real_cli_command`, `terminal.rs:286`). There is no `--continue`, so the agent forgets the previous message, and the session the user resumes (#651, #653) never sees composer prompts.

## Behaviour
- Send writes the prompt into the active tab's running CLI with bracketed paste, then Enter. The conversation is the tab's session, the same one the user sees in the terminal.
- If the tab's CLI is not running, Send starts or resumes the file's session first (#651).
- Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts a newline. The field grows from 1 to 8 lines, then scrolls.
- Up arrow on an empty field (or while browsing) walks this tab's sent prompts, newest first, up to 100. Down arrow walks back and restores the half-typed draft.
- Each tab keeps its draft when the user switches tabs or sessions.
- Pasting a layer reference copied from the canvas inserts a reference chip (#655 format), not raw JSON.
- While a turn is running, Send stays available and the CLI receives the text as it would from the keyboard. The CLI decides whether to queue it.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Two composer messages in a row: the second answer refers to the first. Test with a stub CLI that echoes its session history.
2. History and draft restore work as described.
3. Switching tabs keeps each draft.
4. No `-p`/`exec` one-shot call remains on the composer path.

Depends on: #651, #653, #681.

tasks.title: Agent session files: per-window and per-session paths, cleanup on close, and no full-document JSON on the UI thread
tasks.body:
Three problems in the live agent context sync (`crates/designos-app/src/terminal.rs`, `designos-mcp/src/server.rs`), all verified on `main` at `9f3f7a5`.

1. **Shared `/tmp` files.** Non-test builds still write the global `/tmp/designos-live-context.json` and `/tmp/designos-live-canvas.designos` (`terminal.rs:~804, 816`), and designos-mcp defaults to them (`server.rs:53-61`). Two Studio windows overwrite each other's agent context. #43 covers only the doc-sync fallback.
2. **Session folders never deleted.** `temp_dir()/designos-sessions/p<pid>-tab-N` is never removed outside tests (`terminal.rs:676-680`).
3. **Full-document serialization on the UI thread.** `sync_live_file_context` calls `doc.to_json()` on the UI thread on every mutation, page or selection change for documents up to 25k nodes (`terminal.rs:~800`). This breaks the CLAUDE.md §4 invariant against UI-thread serialization.

## Acceptance criteria
- Context and canvas files live only in the session folder, keyed by window and session id (or the per-file session id of #653). No global `/tmp` path is read or written outside tests; grep proves it.
- Closing a tab removes its session folder unless the session is kept for resume (#653). On launch, folders older than 7 days whose owning process is gone are removed.
- The canvas snapshot is written off the UI thread from a cheap clone, the same pattern the autosave uses. A UI-thread timing test on a 25k-node document shows no frame over 16 ms caused by the sync.
- Two windows with agents attached keep separate contexts (shell test).
